title: Safety and Shipping Review 2026
abstract: The annual review of ship losses, casualties and emerging risks from one of the largest marine insurers. It is where the shadow fleet, GNSS interference and port congestion show up as insurance numbers.

title: OSINT Techniques: Resources for Uncovering Online Information
abstract: The standard practical reference for finding and analysing publicly available information: search methods, social media, virtual machines, custom tools, documentation and ethics. Bazzell rewrites it every year or two, so buy the current edition and treat older ones as history.

title: Oil and Water
abstract: An investigation into the largest known dark fleet run by a single network: at least 56 supertankers carrying Iranian, Venezuelan and later Russian crude to China, using dark voyages, ship-to-ship transfers and GNSS spoofing to hide the oil's origin. A model of how to build a case from AIS, imagery and corporate records.

title: European Union Serious and Organised Crime Threat Assessment 2025: The changing DNA of serious and organised crime
publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
abstract: Europol's four-yearly assessment of organised crime in the EU: the criminal markets, how networks are organised and what is changing, with a strong section on logistics and ports. The reference point for European threat pictures until the next edition.

title: Global Shell Games: Experiments in Transnational Relations, Crime, and Terrorism
abstract: An experimental study of how easy it is to set up an anonymous shell company. The authors posed as consultants and approached nearly 4,000 corporate service providers in more than 180 countries, then recorded who asked for identity documents and who did not. The results still frame how we think about the gaps that let terrorist financing, corruption and arms trading through.

title: Global Organized Crime Index 2025

author.literal: Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime

publisher: Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime
abstract: Scores for 193 countries on criminal markets, criminal actors and resilience, with the methodology published and the data downloadable. The fastest way to get oriented on a country's illicit economy before you read the detail.

title: Empire of AI: Dreams and Nightmares in Sam Altman's OpenAI
abstract: A reporter's account of OpenAI and the race for AI dominance, including the labour in the Global South and the environmental cost behind the products. Useful background for anyone using these tools in intelligence work, and a reminder of where the power sits.

title: The Great Game: On Secret Service in High Asia
abstract: The nineteenth-century contest between Britain and Russia for Central Asia, told through the officers and explorers who fought it. It is the background to borders, grievances and trade routes that are still live, and it is a good story.

title: Maritime Activities Observed Through Open-Access Positioning Data: Moving and Stationary Vessels in the Baltic Sea
abstract: A study that rebuilt Baltic Sea vessel activity from open AIS data alone and came within about 20 percent of results from proprietary data. It is the best evidence we have for when the free sources are enough.

title: The Shadow of the Sun
abstract: Forty years of reporting from across Africa, from independence to the 1990s, by a Polish correspondent who travelled poor and listened. It teaches how to see a place before you analyse it.

title: Rhetoric and Governance under Trump: Proclamations from the Bullshit Pulpit
abstract: An academic study of how rhetoric shaped governance during the first Trump administration, and what it did to institutions. We include it because the language of power is part of the environment analysts report on.

title: Somalia: Economy without State
abstract: How Somalia's economy kept working, and in places grew, without a central government: livestock exports, remittances and trade networks that run on trust and clan. It challenges the assumption that markets need a state, which matters for anyone working on ungoverned spaces.

title: Ghetto at the Center of the World: Chungking Mansions, Hong Kong
abstract: An ethnography of one building in Hong Kong where traders from South Asia and Africa buy phones and clothes to carry home. It is the best short account we know of low-end globalisation, the informal trade that moves goods across the Global South.

title: The New Rules of War: How America Can Win Against Russia, China, and Other Threats
abstract: How war has changed in the twenty-first century and why conventional doctrine keeps losing to it. McFate's "durable disorder", in which states, mercenaries and criminal networks blur together, is the environment much illicit trade work sits in.

title: Global Outlaws: Crime, Money, and Power in the Contemporary World
abstract: An anthropologist follows smuggled goods and money across borders, from African ports to European markets, and shows how illegal trade shapes economics and politics along the way. It is fieldwork rather than statistics, and it reads like it.

title: Unsafe by Design?: A First Look at Security and Privacy Risks in OpenAI's Custom GPT Ecosystem
container-title: Proceedings of the 24th Workshop on Privacy in the Electronic Society (WPES '25)
abstract: An analysis of 14,904 custom GPTs that found most lacked basic protections: system prompts leak, roleplay and phishing attacks succeed, and the marketplace does little about it. Read it before you trust a third-party GPT with case material. The arXiv version is free to read.

title: Berkeley Protocol on Digital Open Source Investigations: A Practical Guide on the Effective Use of Digital Open Source Information in Investigating Violations of International Criminal, Human Rights and Humanitarian Law

author.literal: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
Human Rights Center, UC Berkeley School of Law

abstract: The standard for open source investigations that need to stand up to legal scrutiny: principles, methods, preservation and verification, and the ethics of handling material. If you read one methodology document, read this one.

title: RUSI Maritime Sanctions Taskforce: Insurance and Flag States

author.literal: Royal United Services Institute, Centre for Finance and Security

abstract: Findings from the taskforce's May 2025 meeting of about sixty government and industry members on Russia's shadow fleet: what insurers can do, how to hold flag states to account, and how to target the enablers. Short, and written for people who have to act on it.

title: Treasure Islands: Tax Havens and the Men Who Stole the World
abstract: A readable account of the offshore system: what tax havens are, how they grew and who benefits. It explains the plumbing that most illicit trade investigations eventually run into.

title: Dark Commerce: How a New Illicit Economy Is Threatening Our Future
abstract: An account of how technology changed illicit trade, from drugs and people to wildlife and cybercrime. Shelley shows how these markets connect to each other and how digital anonymity and globalisation let them scale, which is the background every illicit trade analyst needs.

title: AIS Handbook

author.literal: UN Committee of Experts on Big Data and Data Science for Official Statistics, AIS Task Team

abstract: A method handbook for working with AIS data: what the messages contain, how to clean them, how to derive port calls and voyages, and the pitfalls. Written for statisticians, which is why it is careful about what the data can and cannot show.

title: Understanding Terrorist Finance
abstract: A framework for analysing terrorist finance that dispels the popular myths about how groups get and use money. Wittig shows that terrorists work through everyday economic systems rather than a separate shadow finance world, which changes where an analyst should look. Priced for libraries, so borrow it or read it through a university subscription.
